strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Runtime-controlled task.start now admits or replays one explicit retry task from current structured llm_provider_failure evidence.
Retry admission does not call the provider and does not bypass task-run network or sensitive prompt guards.
TaskStarted records bounded llm_provider_failure_retry_provenance without raw prompt, request, response, secret, or file content.
Headless callers can move from retryable provider failure fingerprint to a concrete retry task and next action without stale or duplicate retries.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances llm_provider_execution with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: task.start accepts llm_provider_failure_retry_source and creates or replays exactly one retry task from current structured provider failure evidence and explicit authorization.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M13.1 classified provider failures but left retry creation to external callers, losing provenance and stale-fingerprint safety.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Autonomous callers can identify retryable provider failures but cannot recover through a runtime-owned bounded retry task admission path.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M12.1/M12.2 covered external Mode Pack policy/provenance and M13.1 covered provider failure classification; M13.2 changes retry admission behavior.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing task.start is extended; no new report, status, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. Bounded admission metadata is intrinsic to TaskStartResult and TaskStarted provenance, not a new summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: task.start validates source task/run IDs, terminal Failed status, expected failure fingerprint, retryable failure class, and explicit authorization before creating or replaying one retry task.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Controllers receive retry task/run IDs, failure class, fingerprint, replay flag, and next_action=run_llm_provider_retry_task_explicitly.
answers.milestone_progress: M13 moves from structured provider failure outcomes to runtime-owned provider failure recovery admission.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M13.2 changes deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm task.start retry admission behavior, replay safety, and bounded evidence rather than a wrapper or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: Retryable http_status provider failure admits exactly one retry task through task.start with expected failure fingerprint and explicit authorization
Repeating the same authorized retry admission replays the same retry task/run without creating duplicates
Mismatched failure fingerprint is denied without creating a task
Missing authorization is denied without creating a task
Non-retryable network_not_authorized and configuration failures are denied without creating a retry task
Admission does not append TaskRunning and does not append provider request events

TaskStarted retry provenance and TaskStartResult exclude raw prompt, raw provider response, raw request body, file content, stdout, stderr, commands, environment values, API keys, secrets, absolute paths, and canonical paths
No new RPC, diagnostics wrapper, readiness report, digest, history, status wrapper, preview, automatic retry, provider call during admission, or VSIX-owned provider policy path is added
next_phase_candidate_notes: M13.3 may add explicit retry task.run provenance revalidation before entering provider execution, without automatic retry or guard bypass.
